TRIAGE DIRECTIVE (operator ruling 2026-10-03): this is an IMPLEMENTATION CHORE. Its specification and design are settled and accepted: openspec/changes/decision-0065-capabilities-slice-two/ (merged as 7f0aa4ad, council-cleared in run build-decision-0065-slice-two-co-50ef1e34) and decision 0077 (accepted). Do not re-specify or re-design: classify it `chore` so it goes straight to implement. It is still reviewed by the full engine council. If the settled design cannot be implemented as written, the implement seat reports blocked; triage does not reopen the design.

BUILD DECISION 0065, SLICE TWO — UNIT U6e, one narrow visit, ONE pull request. Branch s2/U6e, cut from main at 41235de5. Recipe claude-flash-dsh-adv.

READ FIRST: design.md's "Slice two units" preamble and your unit (below, verbatim), the tasks your unit closes in tasks.md, the spec deltas it names, operator-ruling-2026-10-03.md, decision 0077 and decision 0065. Units before yours in your row's Dependencies have landed on main.

THE PREAMBLE, verbatim:
## Slice two units

One row is one PR, from main, signed and through the merge queue after the
operator rules. Follow this order. Dependencies are semantic prerequisites,
not simply the preceding row; the independence of U1–U4 is explicit in D9.
No row through U9a lifts the MCP compile fence. U9b is the sole enabling PR.
The lettered splits are required by the checked seams: record schema plus
embedded copy already consumes two files; multi-server wiring crosses runtime,
protocol and adapter data; storage/folding/inspect crosses CLI, protocol,
runtime and pure view. Minimal ledger writing is deliberately pulled into U6.

`contracts/realms.v<N>.schema.json` denotes one exact future file allocated
as **the next realms version after v7** at U5c, including v7's fields. It is
the only intentionally deferred filename number. Every other production path
below is literal. New paths are proposed modules/schemas, not files created
by this document plan. Constructors/registration are counted in their row.
Future tests extend the named suites; capability_broker already exists under
the consolidated CLI integration binary. New capability_artifacts and runtime
capability_ledger/capability_broker_launch modules are registered through the
existing test-only roots (CLI tests/it.rs and runtime tests/it.rs), not new
undeclared binaries. Tests may use child modules of the owning suites to stay
below 2,000 lines; list every test move in unit evidence.

Each row closes exactly its numbered tasks, including tests/mutations and
gate evidence. Test lists below are the allowed owning suites; every row
also updates this change's tasks and later implementation evidence. Measured
witness/compose pins accompany only rows that change their inputs.

YOUR ROW, verbatim:
| U6e | U6d | Serve the filtered protocol; 30.1–30.2 | `crates/brokkr-cli/src/broker.rs`; `crates/brokkr-cli/src/broker/session.rs`; `crates/brokkr-cli/src/broker/rpc.rs` |

YOUR UNIT, verbatim:
### U6e — Serve the filtered protocol

Implement the bounded filtered protocol with private Started/Terminal records. Correlate typed response IDs to method/session state, fix absolute deadlines and bound non-response traffic. Fatal protocol/init/version/limit/timeout outcomes latch CR3 session failure; ordinary tool errors and local denials remain call outcomes. Public serving remains closed until U6f; no unsafe intermediate proxy.

The protocol consumes only U6c8's admitted boxed transport. Startup admission, readiness, handoff and initialization use the same absolute startup deadline; list/call limits remain MB3's. No unboxed child, shell or reconnect path exists. Test missing in-box dependencies separately from protocol corruption and from pre-secret refusals.

Closes tasks 30.1 and 30.2; requirements [MB3](specs/mcp-capability-broker/spec.md), [CC2](specs/capability-call-checkpoints/spec.md), [CR3](specs/capability-response-retention/spec.md), [SC4](specs/slice-two-contracts/spec.md).
Proof: Allow/deny/catalog/version/method controls; wrong-type/late/duplicate/phase IDs, endless progress, cancellation, concurrent calls and persistence failures never forward an unrecorded or uncertain retry. Invalid request shapes/vocabulary and 257-byte names refuse before acceptance; a valid 256-byte ungranted name records one exact denial without truncation.

Owning tests: `crates/brokkr-cli/tests/capability_broker.rs`.

CONTROLLER'S STATE FOR THIS RUN (the-forge-67, 2026-10-12). This is U6e's THIRD run, a REPAIR of ONE finding. It clarifies the commission.

WHY:
- Run 0065-slice-two-unit-u6e-see-the--d6424e8f built U6e (head 5c22affa) under the operator's 2026-10-11 rulings. Its council left one MEDIUM after two reforgings, so it parked.
- The chief confirmed: no security residual and no specification defect; public serving still refuses ServingIncomplete after boxed initialization and listing; the compile fence is unchanged; all 30 broker::rpc tests pass. KEEP all of it.
- The operator ruled on 2026-10-12: REPAIR M1 IN U6E NOW, not deferred to U6f.
- The worktree arrives with the second run's whole attempt applied UNCOMMITTED on current main, including the 2026-10-11 U6e addendum (keep it in your commit). If quality/file-lines.txt was left out, set your files' rows to measured counts.

FIX M1 (MB3's two-second cancellation settlement; design.md about :562's continuing reader; tasks 30.1-30.2; ruling 9):
- rpc/calls.rs (about :353) delegates harness output to session/readiness.rs (about :90), whose polling loop can't read harness input while it writes.
- During a silent active call, a ping with a large valid string ID fills the unread output pipe. A following notifications/cancelled then can't reach Session::cancel until the call or attempt deadline, up to 120 s.
- Make harness writes INCREMENTAL in the serving loop: one loop that keeps reading harness input while output drains, with bounded queues and preserved frame order, and no unbounded buffering (the 1 MiB/8 MiB bounds stand).
- Add a binding regression: an active silent call, blocked harness output (a reader that doesn't drain), then notifications/cancelled. Assert that cancellation settles within 2 s plus a stated scheduling tolerance, with the exact cancellation outcome, no forwarded retry and the ledger consistent. Record an independent compiling removal; for example, the old write-then-read ordering must make it fail.
- Correct evidence/U6e.md (about :433), which recorded the limitation.

CARRIED (record, no action): L1 (SC4 validator duplicated from brokkr-runtime's private binding.rs; sharing needs another crate), L2 (Fatal/Refused Display hand-written; thiserror would need Cargo.toml), L3 (Answered decoded again downstream; carry the parsed outcome on the typed edge result where it fits in your files, otherwise record it). Info: rpc.rs (about :9-11)'s null-handling comment overstates. Correct it.

BEFORE YOU COMMIT, measure these yourself; CI runs them:
- `cargo crap --path <crate>/src`: new functions at CC 15 or below.
- Every new line, error arm and Display text exercised (CI demands 100%).
- Linux-only code behind cfg(target_os = "linux") with a refusing non-Linux stand-in. CI builds macOS.
- Never trace bulk syscalls across a broker process tree in tests.
- Real-box tests skip in your box. The controller runs them on the host at 2 CPUs.

GATES:
- `cargo +1.88 check --workspace --all-targets --all-features`
- quality/ratchet.sh api, files, clones, and baselines origin/main
- `cargo test -p brokkr-cli --lib broker::` and CLI `--test it capability_broker::`, with an owner-only TMPDIR where your sandbox allows
- fmt, clippy, `openspec validate --strict`, typos, and `git ls-files -z '*.md' | xargs -0 lychee --offline --include-fragments --no-progress`

A LOW you can't fix inside your files: record it and do NOT report blocked. Commit everything as ONE signed commit.

RE-VOUCH (the-forge-67, 2026-10-12). Run 0065-slice-two-unit-u6e-see-the--853dc19d delivered U6e as PR #648: M1 fixed, all Linux checks green, and on the controller's host 74 real-box and 81 broker unit tests pass at 2 CPUs. But CI's macOS test job runs past its 30-minute limit every time (two CI runs and three diagnostics). Main's macOS job takes 13-16 minutes, and GitHub keeps no log for a job cancelled at its limit. The controller reproduced the cause on Linux by shrinking every rpc test pipe to macOS's starting 16 KiB (F_SETPIPE_SZ):
- PRODUCT (yours to fix, in your files): the serving loop paces harness writes by sleeping SLICE (100 ms) whenever a write would block. Throughput is therefore one pipe-full per 100 ms: about 640 KB/s with Linux's 64 KiB pipes, about 160 KB/s with macOS's 16 KiB. An 8 MiB answer (MB3's bound) takes about 13 s on Linux and about 50 s on macOS, past the deadlines.
  - Make delivery keep pace with the reader: don't sleep while output is making progress; sleep only when nothing moved in either direction.
  - If the clean fix needs poll(2) readiness, rustix's "event" feature must be added to crates/brokkr-cli/Cargo.toml, which is outside your row. In that case record it as the needed ruling, and land the in-row progress-based fix now.
  - Keep MB3's bounds and the 2-second cancellation settlement (the M1 fix) exactly.
- TESTS:
  - With 16 KiB pipes, an_answer_that_with_the_callers_own_id_passes_mb3s_bound_ends_the_session fails (the harness gets None before the answer).
  - Several tests write to the broker with blocking write_all loops (the "flooded" case near tests.rs :1596, the "stalled" pings near :1621). They block forever if the broker stops reading while its pipe end stays open, which is the likely macOS hang.
  - Make every harness-side write in tests non-blocking (FIONBIO) and deadline-bounded, never a blocking write into a pipe the broker may stop reading.
  - Make sure each session drops its pipe ends when it ends, so writers see EPIPE.
- PROVE IT on Linux with macOS-sized pipes: run broker::rpc with every test pipe shrunk to 16 KiB. You may add rustix's "pipe" feature only if the operator rules on Cargo.toml; otherwise do it as a local, uncommitted experiment and record the result in evidence/U6e.md. All of broker::rpc must pass that way, and finish in normal time.
- Keep everything else. Fix only what's wrong. Commit as ONE signed commit.

STANDING RULINGS. Decision 0065's hold: off by default, no grandfathering; realm-only grants; tools are an abstraction, dialects the concrete; refuse, never reconcile (slice one's operator ruling of 2026-09-23). The MCP compile fence stays in place until U9b. Hosts are Linux and macOS only (decision 0063). Main's code-health rules bind: no `unsafe` in brokkr-runtime; `#[expect(.., reason)]`, never `#[allow]`; clippy's too_many_lines, excessive_nesting and struct_excessive_bools are denied, so split, and only if splitting would widen your unit carry `reason = "baseline 2026-09-29, decision 0065 slice one merged with main; split after #319"`; when a count moves, re-measure quality/'s file-lines, too-many-lines and suppressions (the steps quality/measure.sh uses), witness pins with `BROKKR_BLESS=1 cargo test -p brokkr-runtime --test witness_digests` (or, once #423's single test binary is on your base — crates/brokkr-runtime/tests/it.rs exists — `BROKKR_BLESS=1 cargo test -p brokkr-runtime --test it witness_digests::`), and budgets with scripts/measure-budgets.sh. Where a crate has tests/it.rs, a NEW tests/*.rs file must be registered as `mod <file>;` in that crate's tests/it.rs (layering::test_targets refuses an unregistered one), unless it sets HOME, cwd, env or a global allocator, in which case it is its own [[test]] in Cargo.toml with the reason written there; and `--test <file>` filters become `--test it <file>::` (capability_launch stays its own binary).

RULES. Touch at most the production files your row names; if the real scope exceeds them, STOP and report `oversized` with the split. One exception, the operator's standing rule of 2026-10-09 (operator-ruling-2026-10-03.md): beside a production file in your row that sits at its 800-line ceiling, or is frozen at its quality/file-lines.txt baseline above it, you may add NEW private child modules, declared from that file, in its own module tree and consumed in this unit, without stopping. The same holds beside a row file that your own change would push past 800 lines (extended 2026-10-11). You may also change an EXISTING private child module of a file in your row, in that file's own module tree (extended 2026-10-11). You may move existing code out of the full file into such a child to make room, preferring the code your change touches. Name each new file in your evidence and commit, and set its quality/file-lines.txt row. You may also add a name to an EXISTING re-export in the parent module that declares one of your row's files, where the parent's line count does not change (extended 2026-10-10). Files in any other module tree still mean `oversized`; any public API growth still needs the operator's ruling at PR time (record it, do not stop). Test files are NOT bounded by the row (controller's standing clarification, 2026-10-05): a test anywhere that pins behaviour your unit changes, a validator or fixture swap in another suite, or a new child test module beside an owning suite that sits over its line ceiling is part of your unit — size-neutral wherever a file sits at its quality/file-lines.txt baseline. A LOW finding you cannot fix inside your row's production files: record it in your result and do NOT report blocked for it. Tests assert exact reasons and values, never is_err(); every new test is bound by a compiling mutation that makes it fail, then restored, recorded (test, assertion) in evidence.md. Tick a task in tasks.md only on observed evidence; record results in a NEW file of your own, openspec/changes/decision-0065-capabilities-slice-two/evidence/U6e.md (two lanes deliver units at once, and every unit appending to evidence.md made each pair of pull requests conflict), and do not edit evidence.md itself; write it in prose or a table — never as a bullet list of the standard gate lines (`cargo fmt ...: clean`, `cargo clippy ...: clean`), which earlier evidence files already hold word for word, so the data clone gate refuses it; never edit the tasks.md preamble. Fixtures build on a canonicalised temporary root; no test reads .forge/ or needs an installed provider. Frozen contracts, policy/phase-machine.json, fixtures/, reference/ and extensions/ do not move unless your unit names them. Sign every commit (`git commit -S`; main requires signatures). HEADLESS SEAT: your session ends the moment you end a turn — never run a command in the background, never use Monitor or ScheduleWakeup, run every command in the foreground under the tool's 10-minute limit (suites crate by crate with `timeout 590`, split by --lib/--test if longer), and write your result file before you finish. GATES: cargo fmt --all -- --check; cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings; the suite of each crate you touched; openspec validate --all --strict; typos --hidden; git diff --check; quality/ratchet.sh files and clones. CI also builds and tests on macOS, which this host cannot: Linux-only code (namespaces, mountinfo, /proc, device numbers, Linux-only syscalls) goes behind `#[cfg(target_os = "linux")]` with a non-Linux stand-in that refuses, as broker/session.rs does, and any libc or rustix type you use must be the same type on both (rustix's Dev is u64 on Linux and i32 on macOS; U6c6a's first PR failed to compile there). Keep the session small; commit when the unit is done; never push.

instructions.analyze:
# OpenSpec analyze

Judge duplication, ambiguity, underspecification, house alignment, coverage gaps, and inconsistency across proposal, deltas, design and tasks. Treat the realm house as the constitution. Return each finding with severity and its earliest owning artifact; zero findings is consistent.
instructions.clarify:
# OpenSpec clarify

Judge underspecified areas, unquantified language, missing decisions, capability/delta mismatches, and requirements without adequate scenarios. Return every ambiguity with the evidence needed to settle it; zero findings is clear.
instructions.design:
# OpenSpec design

Write `openspec/changes/<change>/design.md`. Record context, goals and non-goals, decisions with alternatives, risks, migration, and open questions. On return, revise the design and dependent artifacts so no finding is merely acknowledged.

# OpenSpec return

Revise the returned change in dependency order. Encode an answered ambiguity as a scenario, record design choices under `## Decisions`, and keep every dependent artifact coherent. Record a reasoned refusal in the owning artifact.
instructions.implement:

Write `openspec/changes/<change>/tasks.md` as numbered groups of checkboxes. Name the requirement served by every task. On return, repair the breakdown and its requirement coverage before implementation resumes.

# OpenSpec return

Revise the returned change in dependency order. Encode an answered ambiguity as a scenario, record design choices under `## Decisions`, and keep every dependent artifact coherent. Record a reasoned refusal in the owning artifact.

Change location: `openspec/changes/{change}`. Archive operation: ["openspec","archive","{change}","--yes"].

# OpenSpec archive

Folding a change is the last task: run the archive operation named above,
which moves the change directory under `openspec/changes/archive/` and
folds its deltas into `openspec/specs/`. Folding also records which change
wrote which capability, so every capability the change touched carries a
`## Provenance` list.

After the archive operation, open each capability's
`openspec/specs/<capability>/spec.md` that the change touched and append
exactly one line under a `## Provenance` heading held at the end of the
file:

`- \`<archived-directory-name>\` — folded <YYYY-MM-DD>`

`<archived-directory-name>` is the directory the archive operation
created under `openspec/changes/archive/`; `<YYYY-MM-DD>` is the day it
was folded. Append only: never rewrite, reorder or remove an existing
provenance line, because standing truth accumulates and is not edited into
a different meaning. The line is a pointer, not a summary — it names the
change and nothing else, and the why stays in the change directory.

house.content:
This realm is a Rust workspace. Production code is Rust under `crates/`; the
Rust-only architecture is recorded by decision 0009. Semantic changes carry a
decision document with status `proposed` because only the operator accepts one.
Intake seats read `README.md` and decisions 0004 and 0005 before framing a
commission, along with the code and history it touches.

The frozen v1 contracts under `contracts/`, the production table at
`policy/phase-machine.json`, and `reference/` (its schemas included) are
read-only.
A contract change lands as a new version file beside the old one, never as an
edit. The evaluator corpus under `fixtures/` is also frozen and is never
regenerated, only versioned.

Tests are part of every change. Extend the suite that proves the code, run
`cargo test --workspace`, compile `recipes/self`, and leave formatting, clippy,
and the exact-coverage gate clean before reporting success.

Commit completed work with `git` using the repository's message style. Never
push.

The supported hosts are Linux and macOS (decision 0063); WSL2 is Linux. Write
no Windows-conditional code, test or evidence.

## Architecture

Decision 0071 rules how code here is shaped. Build to it, and cite its ruling
numbers in what you judge. Where a gate named below holds a rule, the gate is
the authority, and a finding it would catch is the gate's.

- **Pure core (ruling 1).** `brokkr-core` and `brokkr-view` do no I/O and read
  no clock, environment or randomness. They run no process. Pass `now`, paths
  and environment in as arguments. Effects live in the crates above core and
  view, and are journaled.
- **Enums and data, not traits (ruling 2).** A closed set is an enum matched
  exhaustively, with no wildcard arm that decides behaviour. Anything an
  operator extends is data under `adapters/`, `agents/`, `recipes/` or
  `realms.json`, validated and digested. Add a trait only for a seam whose
  contract spans several operations that must stay consistent with one
  another, reached across a process or service boundary, and name that seam
  in its doc comment. `ProducerTransport` is the one such trait today. A test
  double alone does not make a seam: a single substitutable function is a
  closure seam (`*_with`, `*_in`), which is how the house inverts a
  dependency otherwise.
- **Typed at the edge (ruling 3).** Parse wire, file and harness data once
  into a type, with `serde` and `deny_unknown_fields` where the contract is
  closed. `serde_json::Value` never goes past the edge, into state, or back
  out by string key. Never put `format!("{:?}")` in anything digested or
  journaled. A doubly-optional field or a string vocabulary is a missing enum.
- **Small functions (ruling 4).** New and changed functions stay within 100
  lines, nesting depth 5 and 7 parameters. Cyclomatic complexity follows
  the operator's 2026-09-26 ruling: a function may reach the higher of 15
  and its baseline, so a new function stays within 15, an existing one may
  change freely up to 15, and one already over 15 may only shrink.
  Production files stay within 800 lines and test files within 2,000, and a
  file already over may not grow. Add no new `jscpd` clone in production
  code, test code or data. `quality/` holds the measured baseline. Today's
  offenders carry `#[allow(clippy::…)]`, and #337 converts them to
  `#[expect(clippy::…, reason = "…")]`. Add a suppression only by a ruling,
  and remove it when you fix the function. A new suppression is
  `#[expect(…, reason)]`, never `#[allow]`.
- **Once (ruling 5).** Every fact has one home. A repeated vocabulary, skeleton
  or helper becomes one function or one table. An agent is defined once under
  `agents/`, and seats hire it by reference. A recipe that differs from another
  by a model, a seat or an entry is an `extends` overlay, never a copy. The
  agent library does not yet accept `extends`, and #360 builds it. Until then,
  a variation of an agent lives at the seat that hires it, overridden in a
  recipe overlay. It is never a second agent file that restates the first. A
  copy that must exist, such as a script a bundle pins, is held to its source
  by a test.
- **Nothing unused (ruling 6).** Add no alias, agent, contract version, flag or
  `pub` item without a consumer, and prefer `pub(crate)`. A deprecation names
  the release that removes it.
- **One derivation (ruling 7).** A fact shown on two surfaces is derived once
  in `brokkr-view`. The CLI, the TUI and `ui.html` only paint it. The engine
  never admits anything by a display-crate function.
- **Typed errors (ruling 8).** Return a `thiserror` enum whose `Display` keeps
  the operator's text. Tests match variants and pin each module's text once.
  Add no new `Result<_, String>`.
- **Tests that bind (ruling 9).** Assert exact values or variants, never
  `is_err()` alone. Show that every new test binds: a compiling mutation that
  removes the behaviour must make it fail. Restore the behaviour and record
  the failing test. Share fixtures through builders. Never change the process
  environment without a guard that restores it on unwind. A production guard
  left out because the exact-coverage gate would count it unreachable carries
  a removal-control test for the invariant that makes it unreachable, and the
  comment explaining the omission names that test.
- **The house's patterns (ruling 10).**
  - A harness is a module behind `AdapterKind`. This is the target form;
    today all five kinds share one module, and #347 and #348 build the
    split.
  - A CLI verb is a `Cmd` variant plus a handler.
  - A long parameter list becomes a parameter object.
  - Argv and mount tables are built with a builder.
  - Observing the world is split from deciding on it.
  - Never use a trait-object registry for a closed set.

Judges rate a finding against these rulings by this table, and cite the ruling
number:

- **info:** something a house gate would catch. The gate's verdict is the
  authority.
- **low:** a new or changed function over a ceiling, a rule written a second
  time, an item added without a consumer, or a `Value` carried past its edge
  within one module.
- **medium:** an untyped vocabulary that crosses crates, recipe or agent data
  copied instead of extended, a fact derived a second time on another surface,
  an error matched by its text, or a new test that cannot fail.
- **high or above:** any violation that hides a fail-open path or weakens a
  refusal. It is carried as a security finding.

A principle the implementer bent knowingly, and named with its reason in
`notes`, is still rated, and the judge carries that reason with the finding.

## Release configuration

The release manager prepares the candidate and profile patches; the operator
publishes them. Local validation is preparation work. Remote CI on the final PR
head, publication, channel updates and live-profile verification are handoff
steps, recorded as pending until their remote results exist. Historical
"live from" channel versions and old journal examples are historical facts,
not current-version references to replace.

members.adversarial: Security-only review of c8a0c255 (U6e, including the PR #648 macOS re-vouch), read-only, over base 41235de5. No high, critical or medium finding; no security-hold. INJECTION: clean. Harness frames are parsed once into typed serde shapes (Asked/Called/Greeting/Cancelled) with deny_unknown_fields and depth checked before parsing; server responses are matched by the broker's own typed Id (number != string); the only raw byte concatenation (listing) splices a serde-serialized id and a serde-serialized catalog object, and every other frame is built with serde_json, so escaped newlines/quotes cannot forge a frame; tool names are ASCII-alphanumeric plus ._:/- and <=256 bytes before anything is done. No server-initiated request reaches the harness: ping answered, other requests refused, notifications dropped, each charged to the operation's 1 MiB non-response budget. SECRETS/JOURNAL: the append-only ledger (brokkr-protocol broker/ledger.rs) records only Opened(owner,digest), Started/Terminal(tool,typed Outcome), Closed(typed Disposition); no argument, request id, response body or server prose is recorded, and Fatal::Missing names a plan-granted tool, never server output; no new logging/println in the changed production files. FAIL-CLOSED: production serve still returns Err(ServingIncomplete) after boxed initialize+list (broker.rs:106-107); rpc::initialized drops the Server and Catalog so the box is ended before any byte reaches the harness; calls::served/served_within are expect(dead_code) outside tests and have no production caller (verified by grep), so the call path is unreachable until U6f; every fatal ending latches the closed Failure via Fatal::failure() (Unsupported/Missing->Protocol, Catalog->Response); timeout/cancellation/ledger-limit end the session rather than pass; the non-Linux ready refuses with Unavailable; a broken ledger append leaves no closure so recovery sees only the verified prefix. TAMPER: the ledger is CREATE|EXCL|NOFOLLOW, mode 0600, in the attempt dir; the compile fence and frozen contracts/policy/reference/fixtures are untouched. VERIFIED LOCALLY: cargo test -p brokkr-cli --lib broker::rpc:: -- 35 passed in 13.31 s (every harness-side write non-blocking and deadline-bounded); cargo test -p brokkr-cli --test it capability_broker::protocol:: skips cleanly with the hands-box marker; cargo fmt --all --check and git diff --check clean. LOW S-1 (carried, not a hold): Server::queue has no cumulative cap. During serve's own startup, listed() echoes each server-chosen nextCursor back inside the next tools/list request, so a boxed server that answers guessed sequential ids without ever reading stdin can retain up to ~PAGES_MAX x 8 MiB (~250 MiB) in Server::queued plus a like-sized cursors BTreeSet; once U6f wires calls::served, each accepted call's frame (arguments up to 1 MiB, plus its cancellation) accumulates the same way up to CALLS_MAX, i.e. GiB-scale. design.md:380 explicitly claims no general containment of server memory or denial of service, the growth is bounded by the page/tool/call bounds and freed at session end, and it is a DoS gap that neither hides a fail-open nor weakens a refusal, so it is rated low (reachable now only as a transient startup spike, materially larger when U6f wires the call path); recommend a cumulative Server::queued/cursor cap in U6f. INFO I-1: lifetime::settled latches no cause for Ended::Unrecorded, so a record refused before append with broken still false could let close() write Clean; the call path's Terminal reservation (Outcome::LONGEST) and lifecycle ordering make that unreachable today and lifetime.rs documents it, but U6f should latch a cause or assert the invariant. The prior security seat's S-1/I-1 are confirmed with one correction: the startup path is not ~2 MiB but can reach a few hundred MiB because the server-controlled cursor is echoed into each queued request.
